  GOAL
Add role-aware access control (RBAC) to the Full-Stack FastAPI template. Implement a
user <-> role <-> permission relation in the DB, enforce authorization in the backend,
reflect the same rules in the frontend, add a short-lived (<5min) server-side permission
cache that is invalidated on changes, and migrate the existing `is_superuser` model into a
role with permission "super". Three access levels: Admin, Manager, Member.

LOCKED ARCHITECTURE (contract — all specialists build to this)

Permissions (atomic string names):
  - super        : unrestricted; a holder passes EVERY permission check (back-compat for old superuser)
  - users:read   : list/view any user; view roles list
  - users:manage : create/update/delete users AND change their role assignments ("manage access")
  - metrics:read : view metrics page/endpoint

Roles (seeded, by name):
  - admin   -> {super, users:read, users:manage, metrics:read}
  - manager -> {users:read, metrics:read}
  - member  -> {}   (baseline self-service only: own profile, own password, own items — no special perm)

DB schema (SQLModel, new tables):
  - Permission(id uuid pk, name str unique index, description str|None)
  - Role(id uuid pk, name str unique index, description str|None)
  - RolePermission(role_id fk->role pk, permission_id fk->permission pk)   # M2M
  - UserRole(user_id fk->user pk, role_id fk->role pk)                     # M2M
  - User: DROP the stored `is_superuser` column; add roles: list[Role] via UserRole.

is_superuser compatibility (critical for migration safety + existing tests):
  - UserCreate.is_superuser (default False) stays accepted as INPUT; True => assign admin role on create.
    UserUpdate.is_superuser (optional) stays accepted; True => add admin role, False => remove super-bearing role(s).
    (This keeps init_db(..., is_superuser=True), routes/private.py, and existing tests working.)
  - Add role_ids: list[uuid] | None to UserCreate/UserUpdate for explicit role assignment (admin-only path).
  - UserPublic exposes is_superuser as a COMPUTED field = ("super" in resolved permissions),
    plus new fields roles: list[str] (role names) and permissions: list[str] (resolved perm names).
  - Self-protection "superusers can't delete themselves" => "users with `super` permission can't delete themselves."

Authorization layer (backend/app/api/deps.py):
  - get_current_user unchanged (loads fresh user each request, 400 if inactive) — this already makes
    active-status changes affect existing sessions.
  - resolve_permissions(session, user) -> set[str], served through the cache (below).
  - require_permission(perm) dependency factory: 403 unless perm in resolved perms OR "super" present.
  - Keep get_current_active_superuser == require_permission("super") for back-compat.

Route authorization changes (backend/app/api/routes/users.py etc.):
  - GET  /users/            -> users:read     (admin+manager; member 403; anon 401)
  - POST /users/            -> users:manage   (admin only)
  - PATCH /users/{id}       -> users:manage   (admin only; accepts role_ids)
  - DELETE /users/{id}      -> users:manage   (admin only)
  - GET  /users/{id}        -> self always OK; otherwise users:read
  - POST /utils/test-email  -> keep super (admin only)
  - password-recovery-html-content -> keep super
  - NEW GET /roles/         -> users:read (role selector for admin UI)
  - NEW GET /metrics/ (own router) -> metrics:read (admin+manager). Simple stub: counts (total users,
    active users, users per role). Member 403, anon 401.
  - /users/me, /users/me/password, DELETE /users/me, items/* ownership -> unchanged (member self-service).
  - PATCH /users/me must NOT allow changing roles/permissions/is_superuser (UserUpdateMe has no such fields) — assert this.

Short-lived permission cache (new module, e.g. backend/app/core/permissions.py):
  - In-process TTL cache: user_id -> (frozenset[str] perms, expires_at). TTL default 60s
    (settings.PERMISSIONS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, well under the 5-min requirement). threading.Lock guarded.
  - invalidate_user(user_id) on: user update, role assignment change, deactivation, deletion.
  - invalidate_all() available for role->permission changes.
  - Document the single-process limitation (multi-worker would need Redis) — do NOT implement Redis (scope).

Session/access invalidation requirements (must be true & tested):
  - Deactivating a user -> their existing JWT yields 400 on next request.
  - Demoting a manager to member -> next GET /users/ is 403 (cache invalidated on change, not after TTL).
  - Promoting a member to manager -> next GET /users/ is 200.

Migration (alembic; down_revision = fe56fa70289e, the current head):
  - upgrade(): create permission/role/rolepermission/userrole tables; data-migrate seed the 3 roles,
    4 permissions, and their links; backfill userrole from existing users.is_superuser
    (True->admin, False->member); then DROP users.is_superuser.
  - downgrade(): add is_superuser column back, backfill True for users with admin/super role, drop link tables + role + permission.
  - Must be safe against a populated DB.

Reviewer local exercise:
  - Seed demo users in development only (idempotent, dev-gated): manager@example.com and member@example.com
    with password "changethis" alongside the existing admin@example.com. Document the three logins.

Tests (security-critical focus) — see child task for the checklist. Existing suite (58 tests) MUST stay green.

SEQUENCING
  1. fsf-backend: tests-first (author RBAC checklist) -> model -> migration -> cache -> enforcement -> green.
  2. fsf-frontend: once backend OpenAPI is stable, regenerate client + reflect rules + guard routes + role UI + metrics stub.
  3. fsf-secops: security review of the whole change.

Baseline: existing backend suite is GREEN (58 passed) as of start. FASTAPI_ENV=development, DB at :8071.

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from pydantic import EmailStr, model_validator
from sqlmodel import Field, Relationship, SQLModel


def get_datetime_utc() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RBAC link tables (many-to-many association tables)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class UserRole(SQLModel, table=True):
    user_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="user.id", primary_key=True, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )
    role_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="role.id", primary_key=True, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )


class RolePermission(SQLModel, table=True):
    role_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="role.id", primary_key=True, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )
    permission_id: uuid.UUID = Field(
        foreign_key="permission.id", primary_key=True, ondelete="CASCADE"
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RBAC core tables
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Permission(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    name: str = Field(unique=True, index=True, max_length=255)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    roles: list[Role] = Relationship(
        back_populates="permissions", link_model=RolePermission
    )


class Role(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    name: str = Field(unique=True, index=True, max_length=255)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    permissions: list[Permission] = Relationship(
        back_populates="roles", link_model=RolePermission
    )
    users: list[User] = Relationship(back_populates="roles", link_model=UserRole)


# Shared properties
class UserBase(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr = Field(unique=True, index=True, max_length=255)
    is_active: bool = True
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive via API on creation
class UserCreate(UserBase):
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    # Back-compat input: True assigns the admin (super-bearing) role on create.
    is_superuser: bool = False
    # Explicit role assignment (admin-only path).
    role_ids: list[uuid.UUID] | None = None


class UserRegister(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr = Field(max_length=255)
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive via API on update, all are optional
class UserUpdate(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    is_active: bool | None = None
    # Back-compat input: True adds admin role, False removes super-bearing role(s).
    is_superuser: bool | None = None
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    password: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=8, max_length=128)
    # Explicit role assignment (admin-only path).
    role_ids: list[uuid.UUID] | None = None


class UserUpdateMe(SQLModel):
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    email: EmailStr | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


class UpdatePassword(SQLModel):
    current_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    new_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)


# Database model, database table inferred from class name
class User(UserBase, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)

from collections.abc import Callable, Generator
from typing import Annotated

import jwt
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer

from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core import security
from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.db import engine
from app.core.permissions import resolve_permissions
from app.models import TokenPayload, User

reusable_oauth2 = OAuth2PasswordBearer(
    tokenUrl=f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/login/access-token"
)


def get_db() -> Generator[Session]:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session


SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]
TokenDep = Annotated[str, Depends(reusable_oauth2)]


def get_current_user(session: SessionDep, token: TokenDep) -> User:
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token, settings.SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[security.ALGORITHM]
        )
        token_data = TokenPayload(**payload)
    except InvalidTokenError, ValidationError:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Could not validate credentials",
        )
    user = session.get(User, token_data.sub)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
    if not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Inactive user")
    return user


CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]


def get_current_permissions(session: SessionDep, current_user: CurrentUser) -> set[str]:
    """The effective permission names of the current user (cached)."""
    return resolve_permissions(session, current_user)


CurrentPermissions = Annotated[set[str], Depends(get_current_permissions)]


def require_permission(permission: str) -> Callable[..., User]:
    """Dependency factory: 403 unless the user holds ``permission`` or ``super``."""

    def dependency(current_user: CurrentUser, perms: CurrentPermissions) -> User:
        if "super" in perms or permission in perms:
            return current_user
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403, detail="The user doesn't have enough privileges"
        )

    return dependency


def get_current_active_superuser(
    current_user: CurrentUser, perms: CurrentPermissions
) -> User:
    # Kept for back-compat: equivalent to require_permission("super").
    if "super" not in perms:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403, detail="The user doesn't have enough privileges"
        )
    return current_user

import uuid
from typing import Any

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app.core.permissions import invalidate_user
from app.core.security import get_password_hash, verify_password
from app.models import (
    Item,
    ItemCreate,
    Role,
    User,
    UserCreate,
    UserUpdate,
)


def get_role_by_name(*, session: Session, name: str) -> Role | None:
    return session.exec(select(Role).where(Role.name == name)).first()


def _roles_from_ids(*, session: Session, role_ids: list[uuid.UUID]) -> list[Role]:
    roles: list[Role] = []
    for role_id in role_ids:
        role = session.get(Role, role_id)
        if role is not None and role not in roles:
            roles.append(role)
    return roles


def _resolve_create_roles(
    *, session: Session, is_superuser: bool, role_ids: list[uuid.UUID] | None
) -> list[Role]:
    """Decide which roles a newly created user receives.

    Precedence: explicit role_ids, plus the admin role when is_superuser is set.
    Falls back to the baseline ``member`` role so every user has at least the
    self-service level (mirrors the migration's is_superuser=False -> member).
    """
    roles: list[Role] = []
    if role_ids:
        roles = _roles_from_ids(session=session, role_ids=role_ids)
    if is_superuser:
        admin = get_role_by_name(session=session, name="admin")
        if admin is not None and admin not in roles:
            roles.append(admin)
    if not roles:
        member = get_role_by_name(session=session, name="member")
        if member is not None:
            roles = [member]
    return roles


def create_user(*, session: Session, user_create: UserCreate) -> User:
    db_obj = User.model_validate(
        user_create, update={"hashed_password": get_password_hash(user_create.password)}
    )
    db_obj.roles = _resolve_create_roles(
        session=session,
        is_superuser=user_create.is_superuser,
        role_ids=user_create.role_ids,
    )
    session.add(db_obj)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_obj)
    invalidate_user(db_obj.id)
    return db_obj


def update_user(*, session: Session, db_user: User, user_in: UserUpdate) -> Any:
    user_data = user_in.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    extra_data = {}
    if "password" in user_data:
        password = user_data["password"]
        hashed_password = get_password_hash(password)
        extra_data["hashed_password"] = hashed_password

    # Role-related fields are not columns on User; apply them separately so
    # sqlmodel_update never tries to set the computed is_superuser property.
    role_ids = user_data.pop("role_ids", None)
    is_superuser = user_data.pop("is_superuser", None)

    db_user.sqlmodel_update(user_data, update=extra_data)

    if role_ids is not None:
        db_user.roles = _roles_from_ids(session=session, role_ids=role_ids)
    if is_superuser is not None:
        admin = get_role_by_name(session=session, name="admin")
        if is_superuser:
            if admin is not None and admin not in db_user.roles:
                db_user.roles.append(admin)
        else:
            # Drop any super-bearing role(s).
            db_user.roles = [
                role
                for role in db_user.roles
                if "super" not in {p.name for p in role.permissions}
            ]

    session.add(db_user)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_user)
    invalidate_user(db_user.id)
    return db_user


def get_user_by_email(*, session: Session, email: str) -> User | None:
    statement = select(User).where(User.email == email)
    session_user = session.exec(statement).first()
    return session_user


# Dummy hash to use for timing attack prevention when user is not found
# This is an Argon2 hash of a random password, used to ensure constant-time comparison
DUMMY_HASH = "$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$MjQyZWE1MzBjYjJlZTI0Yw$YTU4NGM5ZTZmYjE2NzZlZjY0ZWY3ZGRkY2U2OWFjNjk"


def authenticate(*, session: Session, email: str, password: str) -> User | None:
    db_user = get_user_by_email(session=session, email=email)
    if not db_user:
        # Prevent timing attacks by running password verification even when user doesn't exist
        # This ensures the response time is similar whether or not the email exists
        verify_password(password, DUMMY_HASH)
        return None
    verified, updated_password_hash = verify_password(password, db_user.hashed_password)
    if not verified:
        return None
    if updated_password_hash:
        db_user.hashed_password = updated_password_hash
        session.add(db_user)
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(db_user)
    return db_user


def create_item(*, session: Session, item_in: ItemCreate, owner_id: uuid.UUID) -> Item:
    db_item = Item.model_validate(item_in, update={"owner_id": owner_id})
    session.add(db_item)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item

from fastapi import APIRouter
from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.api.deps import SessionDep
from app.core.security import get_password_hash
from app.models import (
    User,
    UserPublic,
)

router = APIRouter(tags=["private"], prefix="/private")


class PrivateUserCreate(BaseModel):
    email: str
    password: str
    full_name: str
    is_verified: bool = False


@router.post("/users/", response_model=UserPublic)
def create_user(user_in: PrivateUserCreate, session: SessionDep) -> Any:
    """
    Create a new user.
    """

    user = User(
        email=user_in.email,
        full_name=user_in.full_name,
        hashed_password=get_password_hash(user_in.password),
    )

    session.add(user)
    session.commit()

    return user

"""Unit tests for the short-lived in-process permission cache."""

from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.permissions import (
    invalidate_all,
    invalidate_user,
    resolve_permissions,
)
from tests.utils.user import create_user_with_roles, get_role_by_name


def test_resolve_permissions_caches_and_invalidate_forces_refresh(
    db: Session,
) -> None:
    user, _ = create_user_with_roles(session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    # start from a clean cache entry for this user
    invalidate_user(user.id)

    perms1 = resolve_permissions(db, user)
    assert "users:read" in perms1
    assert "super" not in perms1

    # mutate roles in the DB WITHOUT invalidating the cache
    admin_role = get_role_by_name(session=db, name="admin")
    assert admin_role is not None
    user.roles = [admin_role]
    db.add(user)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(user)

    # still served from cache -> stale (no super yet)
    perms_cached = resolve_permissions(db, user)
    assert perms_cached == perms1
    assert "super" not in perms_cached

    # explicit invalidation forces a fresh resolve
    invalidate_user(user.id)
    perms2 = resolve_permissions(db, user)
    assert "super" in perms2


def test_invalidate_all_clears_every_entry(db: Session) -> None:
    user, _ = create_user_with_roles(session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    resolve_permissions(db, user)
    invalidate_all()
    # after a global flush a fresh resolve still returns the correct set
    perms = resolve_permissions(db, user)
    assert perms == {"users:read", "metrics:read"}


def test_cache_ttl_default_under_five_minutes() -> None:
    # requirement: short-lived, well under the 5-minute (300s) ceiling
    assert settings.PERMISSIONS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS < 300

# Security Review — RBAC implementation (FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-4)

## Verdict: ✅ SHIP — no blocking findings

The RBAC change is well-built and faithful to the LOCKED ARCHITECTURE. The backend is genuinely the authority, there is no privilege-escalation path, invalidation is immediate, the migration is safe, and the cache is correct. Everything below is informational/pre-existing; nothing blocks shipping.

## What I verified against each focus area

**(1) Backend is the authority** — confirmed live. Anon → 401, member → 403 on every protected route; the frontend guards are UX-only (redirect/hide) and the real enforcement is server-side.

| Endpoint | admin | manager | member | anon | Spec |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /users/` | 200 | 200 | 403 | 401 | users:read ✓ |
| `POST /users/` | — | 403 | 403 | 401 | users:manage ✓ |
| `PATCH/DELETE /users/{id}` | — | 403 | 403 | 401 | users:manage ✓ |
| `GET /roles/` | 200 | 200 | 403 | 401 | users:read ✓ |
| `GET /metrics/` | 200 | 200 | 403 | 401 | metrics:read ✓ |
| `POST /utils/test-email` | 201 | 403 | 403 | 401 | super ✓ |

**(2) Privilege escalation — none found.**
- `PATCH /users/me` (`users.py:85`) uses `UserUpdateMe` (only `full_name`/`email`); injected `is_superuser`/`role_ids`/`roles` are silently dropped by Pydantic (verified offline + live: member stayed `[]`).
- `POST /users/signup` → `UserRegister` drops `is_superuser`/`role_ids` before `UserCreate.model_validate` (verified: `is_superuser=False, role_ids=None`).
- Manager self-escalate via `PATCH /users/{self}` → **403** (needs `users:manage`, which manager lacks).
- `crud.update_user` (`crud.py:76`) pops `role_ids`/`is_superuser` before `sqlmodel_update`, so the computed `is_superuser` property is never mass-assigned.

**(3) Session/access invalidation — immediate, no TTL wait** (all verified live and reverted):
- Deactivate member → next request **400 "Inactive user"** (`deps.py:40`, fresh load each request).
- Demote manager→member → next `GET /users/` **403** (cache invalidated in `crud.update_user:102`).
- Promote member→manager → next `GET /users/` **200**.
- All mutation paths invalidate: `create_user`, `update_user`, route `delete_user`/`delete_user_me`; `seed_rbac` → `invalidate_all`.

**(4) Migration `3c2a211a9237`** — safe. Backfill: `is_superuser=true → admin`, else `member`; no unintended grants; `is_superuser` dropped last. Downgrade re-adds the column with `server_default false`, backfills `true` only for `super`-bearing roles, then drops default and tables in FK-safe order.

**(5) IDOR / self-delete** — `GET /users/{id}` (`users.py:166`): self always OK, otherwise `super`/`users:read` required (member→other = 403, member→nonexistent = 403, no existence oracle). Items enforce `owner_id == current_user.id`. Super-holder self-delete blocked on both `DELETE /users/me` and `DELETE /users/{id}`.

**(6) Cache** (`core/permissions.py`) — keyed by `user_id` (no cross-user poisoning), `threading.Lock`-guarded, TTL **60s < 5min**. Deployment runs a **single `fastapi run` worker**, so the in-process invalidation is reliable (the multi-worker limitation is documented and out of scope).
